title: Form Follows Function: Bridging Neuroscience and Architecture

findings.mechanism: High noise levels in healthcare settings.
findings.quote: Edelstein et al. (2008) logged continuous sound levels in emergency and intensive care units and found average levels ranging from 75 to 85 Leq dB(A), with impulse levels from 85 to 100 dB(A), peaking at 120 dB(A) during shift change [10]. Averaged sound pressure levels in intensive care units were up to 10 times greater than conversational speech.

findings.antecedent: Realistic clinical sounds (spatially-distributed multiple sound sources)
findings.consequent: Discrimination of heart sounds, recordings of medication orders, and “sound-alike" pharmaceuticals
findings.mechanism: Auditory masking by competing sounds interferes with critical sound perception.
findings.quote: Demonstrations using spatially-distributed multiple sound sources reveal how discrimination of heart sounds, recordings of medication orders, and “sound-alike" pharmaceuticals are made indistinguishable when masked by realistic clinical sounds [16].

findings.antecedent: Knowing one's location in a 3D VR environment
findings.mechanism: Neural processing related to spatial awareness and cognitive mapping.
findings.quote: Event-related spectral perturbations brainwaves, derived from independent component analysis (ICA), reveal differences in brain dynamics when subjects know their location compared with EEG components when they are lost.

findings.antecedent: Spaces rich with visual cues in a 3D VR environment
findings.consequent: EEG responses in parietal and occipitotemporal cortex
findings.mechanism: Visual information processing for spatial orientation and navigation.
findings.quote: Differences in EEG responses associated with spaces rich with visual cues versus ambiguous spaces devoid of cues were found in parietal and occipitotemporal cortex.

findings.antecedent: Spaces rich with visual cues in a 3D VR environment
findings.consequent: Synchronization in theta waves and desynchronization in lower alpha band of EEG frequencies
findings.mechanism: Involvement of brain regions for navigation and visual orientation.
findings.quote: A significantly stronger synchronization in theta waves and stronger desynchronization in the lower alpha band of EEG frequencies was observed.

findings.antecedent: Disorientation in spaces with less visuospatial information in a 3D VR environment
findings.mechanism: Increased attentional demands due to lack of spatial cues.
findings.quote: Disorientation in spaces with less visuospatial information was associated with increased alpha wave desynchronization, likely reflecting increased attentional demands [20].

findings.antecedent: Ambiguous space (without obvious cues) in a 3D VR environment
findings.consequent: Use of subtle visual cues (shadows, patterned finishes) for navigation
findings.mechanism: Adaptive search for spatial information when explicit cues are absent.
findings.quote: In the case where obvious cue were not presented, subjects looked for any distinguishing features that might indicate location, including shadows around doors, or patterned finishes.

findings.antecedent: Brief exposure (less than 15m) to red light during rest
findings.mechanism: Red light's influence on autonomic nervous system activity.
findings.quote: heart rate variability... was highly significantly different during memory task performance during brief exposure (less than 15 m) to red, bright white, and dark conditions... red light regulated cardiac responses, with appropriate HRV relaxation during rest and activation during the memory task.

findings.antecedent: Brief exposure (less than 15m) to red light during memory task performance
findings.mechanism: Red light's influence on autonomic nervous system activity during cognitive load.
findings.quote: heart rate variability... was highly significantly different during memory task performance during brief exposure (less than 15 m) to red, bright white, and dark conditions... red light regulated cardiac responses, with appropriate HRV relaxation during rest and activation during the memory task.

findings.antecedent: Bright white light with a blue peak
findings.mechanism: Blue-enriched light's influence on autonomic nervous system activity.
findings.quote: bright white light with a blue peak was associated with constant heart rate activation throughout the experiment [28].

findings.mechanism: Different spectral compositions of light influencing neural activity.
findings.quote: brainwaves recorded via a 256 electrode EEG array tended to be different during red versus bright white light conditions in a single subject self-control study [29].

stimuli.description: Immersive 3D virtual reality CAVE with full-scale building models, virtual reality simulations of building scenarios, immersive 3D VR “sound-scenes”, realistic, human-scale, 3D virtual reality environments, and virtual environments with varying visual cues (rich vs. ambiguous).
stimuli.source: Fig. 3.1, Fig. 3.3, Fig. 3.4 and text in sections 3.1, 3.5, 3.6.1, 3.6.2

stimuli.description: Exposure to red, bright white, and dark light conditions, including bright white light with a blue peak.
